label: models/fw_pipejunction.mdl: two pipes meeting at a flanged elbow, bolted

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, C, D where the asset was C, A, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Every view shows the brief's form: two pipe legs meeting at a right-angle elbow, with a flange at each open end. The L outline is the same in FRONT, LEFT, BACK and RIGHT, and the flanges sit where the brief puts them. Nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size for the pipe junction, so there is nothing to be off from. The built size, 34.5 x 12 x 33.5, is a plausible pipe junction. The measured sizeAsked and sizeOff are both null.

M3.reason: Parts the brief names, checked down to the small ones: two pipe legs (present), a flanged elbow (the corner joint is present), and bolts on the flanges. Each end has an octagonal flange (8 sides) with bolt heads on it: four are visible on the top flange in TOP and FRONT-RIGHT, and three on the horizontal end's flange in LEFT. The bolts are small but clear in the side views. No part is missing.

M4.reason: The brief asks for rusted steel and industrial paint, and the asset has it. The pipes are rust-brown with grey-green patches, and the flanges are galvanised grey steel. Each region reads as one material.

M5.reason: Rust mottling on the pipes, edge highlights on the flanges and bolt heads are all present. The brief does not ask for any markings. The detail is a fair match for a worn municipal pipe.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the four readings the judges picked D, D, C and D as the one not made by Valve, and the asset (at C, A, A, C) was never picked, so it passed for one of the game's own.

M7.reason: The brief gives no facing. The piece stands upright on its lower flange, which is the sensible way for a pipe junction to sit on its origin, and the front reads clearly in FRONT.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 276 triangles it is under the 422 that Valve's most complex model of this kind and size spends, so it passes the cap, though it is above the third quartile (156), which is a warning, not a fail. Nothing is open or floating in the visible views. The lower flange's centre looks dark in BACK and BELOW, which may be the pipe end in shadow; it is not charged, but a close look at the underside would settle it.
